problem_statement: When a stepper motion controller raises an event (such as STEPS_COMPLETED or STOPPED) from within an interrupt context, the registered event callback is not always executed. With the previous behaviour, an event generated from ISR context was dropped (only a warning was logged) unless a dedicated option was explicitly enabled per driver instance, so the caller never observed the event and a wait for it times out. The expected behaviour is that the event callback is always delivered, regardless of whether the event originates from an ISR context: the callback must run directly when not in ISR context, and be deferred to a non-ISR context when it is, so that the event is reliably observed.

verification.reason: The statement describes the behaviour change but never names the new Kconfig option CONFIG_STEPPER_CTRL_ISR_SAFE_EVENTS that the tests configure, nor states that it is enabled by default (making the old opt-in per-driver option become an opt-out global option).

problems.detail: The tests set CONFIG_STEPPER_CTRL_ISR_SAFE_EVENTS=n, but the statement never names this Kconfig option. The agent cannot guess the exact name of the new option that replaces the old per-driver CONFIG_STEPPER_*_GENERATE_ISR_SAFE_EVENTS options.

The tests set CONFIG_STEPPER_CTRL_ISR_SAFE_EVENTS=n to test the non-ISR-safe path, implying the new option defaults to y. The statement does not state that the new option is enabled by default, so the agent cannot determine that the behaviour is now opt-out rather than opt-in.

problem_statement_fixed: When a stepper motion controller raises an event (such as STEPS_COMPLETED or STOPPED) from within an interrupt context, the registered event callback is not always executed. With the previous behaviour, an event generated from ISR context was dropped (only a warning was logged) unless a dedicated option was explicitly enabled per driver instance, so the caller never observed the event and a wait for it times out. The expected behaviour is that the event callback is always delivered, regardless of whether the event originates from an ISR context: the callback must run directly when not in ISR context, and be deferred to a non-ISR context when it is, so that the event is reliably observed. This behaviour is controlled by a new Kconfig option CONFIG_STEPPER_CTRL_ISR_SAFE_EVENTS, which replaces the previous per-driver CONFIG_STEPPER_*_GENERATE_ISR_SAFE_EVENTS options and is enabled by default. When CONFIG_STEPPER_CTRL_ISR_SAFE_EVENTS is disabled, the callback must still be invoked directly (without deferral) for every event, but it must not be dropped or suppressed.
